chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamzah ibn Humran, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
The garment does not render the man junub, and the man does not render the garment junub.

key_terms.الثَّوْبُ: the garment or clothing being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الرَّجُلَ: the man, meaning the person in relation to whom the ruling is stated
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man as the subject of the second clause of the ruling
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: renders in a state of janabah; causes the ruling of major ritual impurity to apply

ai.seo_question: Does a garment become junub by contact with a junub person, or can a garment make someone junub?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning janabah and clothing: the state of janabah does not transfer between a person and his garment merely through contact. It indicates that a garment is not judged junub, nor does a garment make a person junub.
